descs.t: A Trump supporter was stabbed outside President Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio, and video shows the knife still lodged in the victim's back. Reports say police have one suspect in custody. We go through what the footage shows, what police have said and what is still unconfirmed.

A Trump supporter was stabbed outside the Chillicothe, Ohio rally while Trump spoke inside, on a night already full of hecklers and ejections. Police reportedly have one suspect in custody. We look at what is known, what is claimed online, and why the coverage matters.

A Trump supporter was stabbed outside the Ohio rally in Chillicothe, with the knife still in the victim's back on video. Political violence at a rally is an attack on everyone's freedom to take part. We go through the footage, the arrest and what it says about where this campaign season is heading.

intro.plain: Last night outside Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio, a Trump supporter was stabbed, and video shows the knife still lodged in the victim's back. Reports say police have one suspect in custody. Inside, Trump was dealing with hecklers. Let's go through what we actually know. Chat, have you seen the video, and what do you want answered first?
intro.mid: A Trump supporter was stabbed outside the Ohio rally in Chillicothe last night, knife still in the back, on camera. Police reportedly have a suspect in custody. This came on a night when the rally was already being interrupted by hecklers. So how is this being covered, and how should it be? Chat, is this getting the attention it deserves?
intro.bold: Someone went to a Trump rally in Chillicothe, Ohio last night and left with a knife in their back. It is on video. Police reportedly have a suspect. I don't care who you vote for: stabbing people over politics is an attack on all of us. Chat, tell me honestly, would this be wall to wall coverage if the roles were reversed?

hook.plain: A Trump supporter stabbed outside the Chillicothe rally, the knife still in their back on video. Here is what police say and what is still unknown.
hook.mid: Hecklers inside, a stabbing outside. The Ohio rally video shows a knife still lodged in a Trump supporter's back. Here is what we know so far.
hook.bold: The knife was still in his back when the camera found him. A Trump supporter stabbed outside an Ohio rally. This is political violence, and it has to be named.

descs.t: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into Mary Peltola's Senate campaign over an alleged scheme to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot against Senator Dan Sullivan. The move follows New York Times reporting, and reports say the DOJ is also investigating. We walk through what was reported, who is involved and what it means for voters who already cast early ballots.

Mary Peltola calls the same name candidate story a distraction, while Alaska's governor and reportedly the DOJ are now investigating her campaign. Critics say ballot stacking is legal, supporters of Senator Dan Sullivan call it voter fraud. We look at the New York Times report, the role reported for national Democrats and where the Alaska Senate race goes from here.

National Democrats reportedly spent months hunting for another Dan Sullivan to put on Alaska's Senate ballot, and now the governor has ordered a probe. JD Vance says Peltola is trying to steal a Senate seat and Trump wants her prosecuted. We break down the reported scheme, the investigations and why thousands of early votes are now in question.

intro.plain: Alaska's governor has just ordered an investigation into Mary Peltola's Senate campaign. The allegation is that her side recruited a second Dan Sullivan to confuse voters in the race against Senator Dan Sullivan, and reports say the DOJ is looking at it too. Early ballots are already in. So tell me in the chat: should Alaska reprint these ballots?
intro.mid: Mary Peltola calls it a distraction. Alaska's governor calls it serious enough to investigate. The New York Times reported her campaign hunted for a second Dan Sullivan to put on the ballot, and now the DOJ is reportedly involved. Some say ballot stacking is legal. Drop it in the chat: is this a dirty trick or a crime?
intro.bold: This is wild. Democrats reportedly went looking for anyone in Alaska named Dan Sullivan, just to confuse voters against the real Senator Dan Sullivan. Now the governor has ordered a probe, Vance says she is trying to steal a seat, and Trump wants Peltola prosecuted. Thousands already voted. Chat, should Peltola drop out of this race?

hook.plain: Alaska's governor has ordered an investigation into a second Dan Sullivan on the Senate ballot. Here is what was reported, who is involved and what happens next.
hook.mid: Two Dan Sullivans on one Senate ballot, early votes already cast, and now an investigation. Is this legal ballot stacking or voter fraud? Let's look at the evidence.
hook.bold: They reportedly searched Alaska for anyone named Dan Sullivan to trick voters. Now Peltola's campaign faces a governor's probe and a reported DOJ investigation. Here is how it unravelled.

descs.t: The Texas Senate race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico is tightening. Republican Don Huffines warns Democrats are out-voting Republicans in early voting for the first time, and one poll shows Talarico ahead 49% to 43%. We go through the polls, the early vote and the campaign push by JD Vance.

Is Texas really in play for Democrats? A poll puts James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton 49% to 43%, CNN polling shows Democrats up 6, and a Republican warns of a swing of nearly 600,000 votes in early voting. We weigh what the numbers can and cannot tell us, and Paxton's plan to abolish property taxes.

Republicans are sounding the alarm in Texas. Early voting, new polls and a rushed visit from JD Vance all point to a Senate race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico that could reshape Washington. We go through the numbers, the competing pitches on taxes and healthcare, and what a flip would mean.

intro.plain: Texas. The Senate race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico is suddenly close. A Republican, Don Huffines, says Democrats are out-voting Republicans in early voting for the first time, and one poll has Talarico up 49 to 43. JD Vance is campaigning in Texas. Chat, do you trust these early numbers?
intro.mid: Is Texas actually in play? One poll has James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton 49 to 43, CNN has Democrats up 6, and a Republican is warning his own side that they are losing Texas. Paxton's answer is to abolish property taxes. Chat, is this real or is it a polling mirage?
intro.bold: A Republican just wrote: we are losing Texas. Early voting, new polls, JD Vance flying in. If Texas flips, the whole map changes. Paxton promises to abolish property taxes, Talarico runs on healthcare for all. Chat, which pitch wins Texas, and are Republicans right to panic?

hook.plain: One poll has Talarico ahead of Paxton 49 to 43, and a Republican says Democrats lead early voting in Texas. Here is what the numbers show.

hook.bold: Texas, the biggest red state in America, and Republicans are panicking. The polls, the early vote and what a flip would mean for Washington.

descs.t: Barack Obama returned to his Cheesecake Factory joke about Donald Trump's White House, saying the president was not bothered by the Saddam Hussein comparison but was upset about the restaurant line. We play the riff, the responses from Trump allies and what it says about the midterm campaign.

Obama says the Trump White House mobilized a whole of government response to his Cheesecake Factory joke, not to inflation. We look at why Obama keeps hitting this line on the campaign trail, how Trump's side answered, and whether it lands with voters.

Barack Obama has turned a Cheesecake Factory joke into a campaign weapon, accusing Trump's White House of caring more about a punchline than inflation or corruption. We go through the riff, the backlash from Trump allies and who comes out of this fight looking stronger.

intro.plain: Obama is back on the Cheesecake Factory joke. Tonight he said the president wasn't even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison, but was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory, and that the White House mobilized a whole of government response to that joke, not to inflation. Chat, did this joke land or not?
intro.mid: Barack Obama is milking his Cheesecake Factory line. He says Trump's team ignored the Saddam Hussein comparison and the corruption charge, and went after the restaurant joke instead. Trump allies are firing back with jokes of their own. Chat, is this smart campaigning or a distraction from real issues?
intro.bold: Obama says the Trump White House fought his Cheesecake Factory joke harder than it fought inflation. Trump's side says Obama is in damage control. One thing is clear: a dessert joke is now a midterm talking point. Chat, who won this round, Obama or Trump?

hook.plain: Obama says Trump wasn't mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison, only the Cheesecake Factory. Here is the full riff and the response.
hook.mid: A whole of government response, not to inflation, but to a joke. That is Obama's charge against Trump. Does it hold up?
hook.bold: Saddam Hussein? Fine. Cheesecake Factory? War. Obama just turned a joke into a weapon against Trump's White House, and both sides are swinging.

descs.t: Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate under criminal investigation, has landed in Miami after leaving Brazil despite a Supreme Court passport seizure order. A now deleted post called him the president elect, and an ally disowned it. We go through what is known about his escape and what comes next.

Flavio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's runoff to Lula and then left the country in defiance of a Supreme Court order, landing in the United States. The New York Times reports Trump and his aides helped him enter. We look at the escape, the deleted president elect claim and the pressure now on Washington.

Flavio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's election, slipped a Supreme Court travel ban and claimed from Miami to be the true president elect, before the post vanished. We ask whether the United States should be a refuge for a politician running from investigations, and what this means for Brazil's democracy.

intro.plain: Brazil. Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's presidential runoff and is under criminal investigation, has landed in Miami after leaving despite a Supreme Court order seizing his passport. A post declaring him the true president elect was deleted, and an ally disowned it. Chat, should the US send him back?
intro.mid: Decoy cars and a jet waiting across the border. That is how reports describe Flavio Bolsonaro's escape to Miami after losing to Lula. The New York Times says Trump's aides helped him enter. Then came the deleted president elect claim. Chat, is Washington making a mistake here?
intro.bold: He lost the election, he fled a court order, he claimed to be president from Miami, and then the post disappeared. Flavio Bolsonaro's week is wild. But the real question is ours: should America shelter a politician running from investigations? Chat, yes or no?

hook.plain: Flavio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's election and landed in Miami in defiance of a Supreme Court order. Here is what we know.

descs.t: Israel's election count is complete: Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48 and the Arab parties 19, with 61 needed for a majority in the Knesset. Netanyahu has complained to the Election Commission that Qatar and Turkey sent money to get Arab citizens to vote. We go through the numbers and the possible coalitions.

Likud is again the largest party, but Netanyahu's bloc stands at 53 seats, short of the 61 needed, and UTJ is reportedly ready to back Eisenkot. Netanyahu accuses Arab parties of stealing votes and points to Qatar and Turkey. We weigh the claim and map who could form Israel's next government.

Israel's election has ended in deadlock, and Netanyahu says Qatar and Turkey money helped push Arab turnout. If foreign regimes are buying influence in a democracy's vote, that is a serious charge that needs proof. We go through the final count of 53, 48 and 19, the claim, and every realistic path to a government.
